paragraphs: CP Group designs, manufactures, installs, and services sorting machinery for the waste and recycling industry. It sells turnkey systems for both new material recovery facilities and retrofits of existing ones. A project management team handles third parties, scheduling, shipping, and installation.

Designing a facility begins with collaborative design meetings, cost reviews, and civil and electrical considerations. The equipment itself is engineered and manufactured in the United States. The shop has 115,000 sq. ft. of manufacturing space and 435,600 sq. ft. of storage on 9 acres. At startup and commissioning, the team goes over compliance, operations, and safety with the customer. Support afterward covers spare parts, process upgrades, and troubleshooting.

The company dates its machinery to the invention of the first commercial aluminum can flattener in 1977, and its name to Can Pac. It later acquired Krause Manufacturing, which makes construction and demolition separation equipment, and Advanced MRF, a specialist in intelligent motor controls and data acquisition. It says it owned and operated a material recovery facility for over 25 years, processing half of the city of San Diego's curbside recycling. That adds up to nearly 50 years of hands-on experience by its own account.
